rollback_node: 1943-10-28 operation start before the Naf crossing
purpose: Reconstruct the Bengal/Arakan land campaign with the v047 integrated Japanese land+vehicle system. Separate physical vehicles, serviceability, terrain, damage class and repair/reappearance before changing casualties or timing.

causal_independence_from_GALVANIC.reason_for_reaudit: The same missing Japanese land-hardware/vehicle layer found at Tarawa was also absent from the Bengal event ledger. Tarawa's numeric casualty delta is not copied to Bengal.

fixed_operational_inputs.main_formation: Japanese 55th Division with traced engineer, mountain-artillery, communications and theater transport support
fixed_operational_inputs.late_reinforcement: 54th Division advance/rear/logistics elements increase only in mid/late December; no full early-November combat division

armored_force.unverified_light_recon_sensitivity: 0-4 tankette/armored-car class vehicles may exist in rear/security roles, but they receive zero centered combat credit without a dated unit trace

fixed_operational_inputs.allied_AFVs: Retain the old 5-10 loss band. British/Commonwealth local armor is limited and terrain/bridge constrained; no new tank duel is created.
fixed_operational_inputs.coastal_LOC: Akyab -> small coastal ship/barge -> Naf/Teknaf/Cox's -> Daihatsu/small craft final delivery

front_supply_band_tpd.rule: Vehicle reliability improves last-mile continuity inside the established band; it does not add tonnage to the sea spine or erase zero-output nights.

land_vehicle_OOB.scope: 55th Division organic motor transport plus specifically attached engineer/communications/Army-area road transport available to the operation; excludes landing craft, coastal vessels, animals and late 54th Division elements
land_vehicle_OOB.interpretation: The broad physical band is consistent with a standard Japanese division's roughly 500 organic-vehicle order of magnitude, then bounded for theater loss, attachments and the mixed motor/draft character of division transport. It is not an exact archival vehicle return.

branch_process_effect_already_inside_ser.dispatchability_relative: +5-12% where roads, fuel, drivers and spares exist
branch_process_effect_already_inside_ser.average_extra_dispatchable_vs_historical: about 20-45 vehicles across the campaign, concentrated in trucks, light tractors, prime movers and engineer plant

terrain_and_reappearance.Naf_Teknaf_Ukhia: river crossings, weak tracks, residual wet-season mud and fragmented unloading constrain wheels; repair access is intermittent
terrain_and_reappearance.Cox_Chakaria_Chiringa: best road-axis interval; workshops and coastal resupply make 24-72h recovery most credible
terrain_and_reappearance.Dohazari_Sangu_Karnaphuli: bridges, ferries, demolitions, artillery and air interdiction again dominate; vehicles support guns/engineers and rear distribution rather than off-road maneuver
terrain_and_reappearance.allowed_24_72h_reappearance_relative: 1.20-1.40x historical-equivalent for reachable repairable wheeled/prime-mover faults on the road axis
terrain_and_reappearance.blocked_upper_band: Do not use 1.6x: broken bridges, rivers, mud, Allied air activity and workshop displacement prevent a maintained open-road formation ceiling.
terrain_and_reappearance.combat_role: transport artillery ammunition and engineer stores, move observation/communications parties, tow or reposition guns, evacuate wounded, restore roads/bridges and keep the coastal-to-road handoff continuous

damage_classification.rule: Temporary mission-kills and repaired vehicles are not added to permanent losses. Destroyed, drowned, captured or abandoned-behind-front vehicles never reappear.

phase_results.change_vs_v001: Teknaf center moves from 5 Nov to late 4 Nov; Ukhia center remains 14 Nov but its upper tail contracts by about one day.
phase_results.mechanism: Fewer common transport/tractor dropouts and more reliable engineer/communications equipment; river and terrain limits remain.

phase_results.change_vs_v001: Cox's Bazar capture centers late 20 Nov instead of 21 Nov. The following conversion pause remains necessary.
phase_results.mechanism: Improved road-axis dispatchability keeps artillery/ammunition/engineer packages together; the coastal tonnage ceiling is unchanged.

phase_results.change_vs_v001: Dohazari attack begins 2 Dec and capture centers early 5 Dec, about 12-24 hours earlier.
phase_results.mechanism: Registered/corrected fire, tactical communications, prime movers, engineer plant and short coastal insertion form one cycle. Landing-package gains were already counted and are not added again.

phase_results.change_vs_v001: Crossing loss falls modestly and the city-entry window shifts to late 14 Dec-early 15 Dec, centered late 14 Dec.
phase_results.mechanism: Better engineer plant uptime, wire/radio reliability, ammunition issue and repairable vehicle return improve execution. British demolition begins in time and prevents a clean port seizure.

revised_casualties.interpretation: The exchange shifts toward Japan but not by the Tarawa ratio. Most Bengal fighting is moving, visibility-limited and supply-constrained, so only traced prepared-fire, artillery movement, communications, engineering and pursuit windows receive the branch effect.

Japan.note: Landing-craft and aircraft bands are unchanged because the old settlement already used the dated amphibious/air allocation layers; the v047 vehicle correction is not stacked onto them.

operational_outcome.Chittagong_capture: late 1943-12-14 to early 1943-12-15; centered late 14 Dec
operational_outcome.British_field_army: not annihilated; 5th and 26th withdraw, 7th escapes with most personnel but slightly fewer stragglers and more heavy equipment lost
operational_outcome.port_condition: heavy demolition still succeeds; no immediate high-throughput Japanese port
operational_outcome.year_end_japanese_state: 55th Division remains exhausted but has about 300-600 more effective personnel available and 20-45 more dispatchable vehicles than implied by v001; defensive regeneration is modestly earlier, not an automatic Feni offensive
operational_outcome.1944_front: Feni-Comilla-Agartala stalemate hardens. No realized Japanese drive beyond Chittagong before or after year-end without a new supply/air/force gate.

unchanged_dependencies: GALVANIC carrier, surface, submarine and ground results
Bengal first-line/secondary carrier centered commitment zero
Fuso/Yamashiro and Ise/Hyuga old-battleship rotation method
late-January/early-February Feni-Comilla stalemate and Central-Pacific priority for further Kinsei fighter allocation
